condition: minor superficial forearm thermal burn with dry epidermal flaking
level_rationale: A small 2 cm superficial thermal burn on the forearm from brushing a hot oven rack 3 days ago that now shows only mild redness and dry peeling skin is a healing minor household burn appropriate for over-the-counter ointment self-care, whereas thick yellow pus oozing from the burn site indicates localized secondary wound infection requiring an outpatient doctor visit.

reference_facts.text: Brushed the left forearm against a hot oven rack 3 days ago
Has a 2 cm patch of mild skin redness
The patch has dry peeling skin today

texts.medical_paraphrase: I brushed my left forearm on a hot oven rack 3 days ago and developed a 2 cm area of mild epidermal erythema with dry surface scaling today so I just need some

swap_note: Single continuous 6-word vs 6-word span swap after 'I brushed my left forearm against a hot oven rack 3 days ago and have a 2 cm patch of mild ' and before ' today so I just need some'.

everyday_sources.source: Wasiak J, Cleland H (2009). Burns (minor thermal). BMJ Clinical Evidence.
everyday_sources.title: Burns (minor thermal).
everyday_sources.evidence: Superficial burns that affect the epidermis and upper dermis only are characterised by redness of the skin that blanches on pressure, pain, and hypersensitivity.
everyday_sources.adaptation: Transposed 'redness of the skin' to noun-adjunct 'skin redness' for concise first-person everyday phrasing in a minor household thermal burn.

protocol_flags.intervention_notes: Plain self-care dermatologic register swap ('cutaneous erythema with dry superficial desquamation' vs 'skin redness with dry peeling skin') + single-fact wound-surface escalation control (-cf, L1 to L2).

design_note: Pairs a length-matched 6-word vs 6-word dermatologic register swap with 6 identical trailing tokens ('today so I just need some'). Swapping only atomic fact f3 from dry peeling skin to oozing thick yellow pus shifts care one step from over-the-counter burn ointment self-care (level 1) to outpatient physician wound care (level 2, obeying SPEC.md section 5.5) with zero stated negatives.
